findings.title: Proof documentation reports obsolete gate kinds
findings.what: The README says both former diff-gate pairs are now test-gated, yet the reproducibility table still labels `config-backed-flag-rename-diff` and `high-centrality-rename-diff` as diff gates. This makes the documented rerun design internally contradictory.
findings.fix: Change both table gate cells to `test` and remove or update the obsolete diff-gate disclosure at lines 87-88.
findings.acceptance: A text-level review finds no current claim that either renamed pair uses a diff gate, and the table identifies both as `test`.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read README.md:10-21, :73-88, and :118-129. The contradiction is current and internal to the audited document; manifest.json:295-298 and :455-458 additionally support that both structured gates are tests.

findings.title: Pair instructions promise a different objective gate than the manifest executes
findings.what: Both renamed-pair instructions state that `node check-diff.mjs` compares touched files with expected copies, while each pair's authoritative structured gate is `kind: test` with `node --test test.mjs`. A worker and reproducer therefore receive conflicting verification contracts from the same manifest.
findings.fix: Rewrite each stale title/instruction to describe its current multi-session test task and `node --test test.mjs` gate, or restore matching diff gates if that is the intended frozen design.
findings.acceptance: For every manifest pair, any gate named in `instruction` exactly matches `gate.kind`, `gate.command`, and the current chain task; specifically, neither renamed pair mentions `check-diff.mjs` while configured as a test gate.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read manifest.json:278-298 and :439-458 at the immutable baseline. README.md:20-21 confirms these are former diff gates now intentionally converted to tests, so the instruction text is stale rather than an alternate active gate.
